finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and saves it. Any user can set privileged or internal fields such as role, isAdmin, id, email-verified flags, or tenant/org id, which allows privilege escalation or account takeover. The sibling route PUT /me/profile (line 11) destructures only displayName and bio, which shows the intended allowlist. Whether the saved fields matter depends on the user model, which isn't in this repo.
finding.source: req.body of PUT /me (any authenticated low-privilege user)

trace.note: PUT /me handler receives attacker-controlled JSON body
Object.assign merges every body key into req.user with no field allowlist
The mutated user is persisted via req.store.save
The full user object is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: There is no field allowlist, schema validation, or role check in this file. The auth middleware that sets req.user is not in this repo, so I only know the route needs an authenticated user. The sibling route PUT /me/profile (lines 10-15) restricts fields, so it is safe from this. Object.assign onto a plain object with a JSON.parse'd body does not pollute the prototype, because __proto__ becomes an own property, so I did not report prototype pollution.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation and users.js:6 saves it, while the sibling route at users.js:11 allowlists fields. The one caveat is that the user model and store.save are outside this repo, so which fields are privileged is unknown.
